old: President Reagan then made Chun the first foreign leader he hosted (1981).
new: President Reagan then made Chun one of the first foreign leaders he hosted (February 1981).
problem: Chun visited on February 2, 1981; Jamaica’s Edward Seaga was the first foreign leader Reagan hosted (January 27–29, 1981).

old: the Senate investigated the “merchants of death” in the 1930s (the Nye Committee) and the revolving door in 1959.
new: the Senate investigated the “merchants of death” in the 1930s (the Nye Committee), and a House Armed Services subcommittee investigated the revolving door in 1959.
problem: The 1959 hearings on retired officers hired by defense contractors were held by the House Armed Services Subcommittee for Special Investigations (Hébert), not the Senate.
sources: House Armed Services Committee, Subcommittee for Special Investigations, Employment of Retired Military and Civilian Personnel by Defense Industries: Hearings (1959)

old: Congress passed short extensions in April 2026 amid disputes over adding a warrant requirement for searches of Americans’ data; a secret court opinion found compliance problems.
new: Congress passed short extensions in April 2026 amid disputes over adding a warrant requirement for searches of Americans’ data, then let the law lapse on June 12, 2026; collection continues under existing court certifications, which run to March 2027, and no renewal had passed by late October. A secret court opinion found compliance problems.
problem: Outdated: after the April stopgaps Section 702 lapsed on June 12, 2026 and had not been reauthorized as of late October 2026, with collection continuing under certifications until March 2027.

old: Counts of bases vary wildly by definition: about 128 major bases in about 49 countries,
new: Counts of bases vary wildly by definition: at least 128 bases in at least 51 countries (a Congressional Research Service count),
problem: The CRS count is “at least 128 overseas bases in at least 51 countries” (68 persistent bases and 60 other sites), not 128 “major” bases in 49 countries.

old: which is why base counts range from about 128 major bases to around 750 sites
new: which is why base counts range from at least 128 bases (a CRS count) to around 750 sites
problem: CRS counts at least 128 overseas bases, of which only 68 are persistent bases; calling all 128 “major” misstates the source.

old: Israel is the largest cumulative recipient of US military aid since WWII (over $300 billion adjusted for inflation, by CRS counts)
new: Israel is the largest cumulative recipient of US aid since WWII, most of it military (about $300 billion adjusted for inflation, by CRS counts)
problem: CRS gives about $298 billion in constant 2024 dollars for all US aid to Israel in 1946–2024 ($174 billion in current dollars), a figure for total aid, not military aid alone, and not “over $300 billion.”

old: 'Over $300 billion, inflation-adjusted (CRS), the most of any country'
new: 'About $300 billion, inflation-adjusted (CRS), the most of any country'
problem: CRS estimates about $298 billion (constant 2024 dollars) for 1946–2024, not over $300 billion.

new: These are permanently assigned active-duty military personnel from the Pentagon’s own June 2025 count.

old: 'Stationed in five allied countries (Belgium, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Turkey)'
new: 'Stationed in five allied countries (Belgium, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Turkey), and reportedly in Britain again since 2025'
